sections.text:
¹ De libro Ammonii Alexandrini agitur, (cf. Catal., II, p. 81, n. 1 ; p. 182) si Steinschneidero credimus, qui de illo Minenid alias Hirmenus disputat l. c., p. 365, n° 14.
² Ibrahim ben Jahjâ el Zarqâlî natus Cordubae circa a. 1029 p. C. composuit celeberrimas tabulas astronomicas quae dicuntur Toletanae et a Gerardo Cremo- nensi versae vel potius ordinatae sunt; cf. Steinschneider. l. c., p. 367, § 17; Suter, op. cit., p. 109, § 255.
³ Est Liber de constitutione astrolabii Masallae (v. infra n. 5) fortasse a Iohanne Hispalensi translatus; cf. Steinschneider, p. 377.
⁴ Tractatus Hermani Contracti De mensura Astrolabii, incipiens verbis ss. denuo editus est Parisiis a. 1853 in Patr. Lat., t. CXLIII, p. 382; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 371, § 29.
⁵ De Masch-Allah vide supra,p. 87, n. 3. Scriptum eius De compositione astrolabii latine inde ab a. 1512 saepius editum est; cf. Steinschneider. p. 376, § 37 b.
⁶ Revera opus de astrolabio astronomi Cordubensis († 1007 p. C.) Maslama ben Ahmed el Madjrîti quod in codicibus quibusdam latinis incipit verbis : Primum capitulum astrolabii in inventione nominum... Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 374; Suter, op. cit., p. 76, § 176.
sections.en:
¹ It is treated concerning the book of Ammonius of Alexandria, (cf. Catal., II, p. 81, n. 1 ; p. 182) if we believe Steinschneider, who disputes concerning that Minenid otherwise Hirmenus l. c., p. 365, n° 14.
² Ibrahim ben Jahjâ el Zarqâlî born at Cordoba around the year 1029 A.D. composed the most famous astronomical tables which are called Toledan and were translated or rather ordered by Gerard of Cremona; cf. Steinschneider. l. c., p. 367, § 17; Suter, op. cit., p. 109, § 255.
³ It is the Book concerning the constitution of the astrolabe of Masalla (see below n. 5) perhaps translated by John of Seville; cf. Steinschneider, p. 377.
⁴ The treatise of Herman the Cripple Concerning the measure of the Astrolabe, beginning with the words above was edited anew at Paris in the year 1853 in Patr. Lat., t. CXLIII, p. 382; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 371, § 29.
⁵ Concerning Masch-Allah see above, p. 87, n. 3. His writing Concerning the composition of the astrolabe in Latin from the year 1512 was edited more often; cf. Steinschneider. p. 376, § 37 b.
⁶ In truth the work concerning the astrolabe of the astronomer of Cordoba († 1007 A.D.) Maslama ben Ahmed el Madjrîti which in certain Latin codices begins with the words: The first chapter of the astrolabe in the invention of names... Cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 374; Suter, op. cit., p. 76, § 176.

summary.headline: Astrological and Astrolabe Treatises
summary.text: Discussion of astronomical and astrological books, including Auxigem’s Almanach, Minenid’s work for Ptolemy’s daughter, and Azarkel’s correction based on Arab years and Toledo. It then lists astrolabe and planisphere treatises translated or attributed to John of Seville, Herman the Cripple, Messahalah, and Maslama al-Majriti.
